* 1. bind-input
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: types/bind-input
:FILE: src/graphden/input/core.clj
:LINE: 130
:MINS: 1.4
:END:

The structured-input transition begins with a pure binding algebra, not yet used by production execution. A partial record binds declared child fields; a whole value or reference occupies its subtree. Stable field paths reject overlapping bindings without executing references. Expected types remain available for later value/HOF classification.

* 20. analyze-effective-input
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: types/analyze-effective-input
:FILE: src/graphden/input/analysis.clj
:LINE: 151
:MINS: 2.9
:END:

Builds an offline graph of evaluated reference uses. Each use has a binding-ID scope; scoped overlays must fit its target's unoccupied fields. Identity refs do not import target inputs, and callable producers expose constructor inputs. Required addresses and typed projections expose their source inputs. Metadata narrows contracts; value cycles reject. Callable plans separate invocation parameters and captures by origin. Deferred field/container obligations remain explicit. Stored-value resolvers consume their own literal argument without capturing ambient caller fields; execution remains inactive.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/input/analysis.clj::(defn analyze-effective-input][src/graphden/input/analysis.clj:151]]

[[file:glossary.org::#term/unification][Unification]] finds substitutions for [[file:glossary.org::#term/unification][type variables]] that make two type expressions compatible. The [[file:glossary.org::#term/unification][occurs check]] prevents a variable from being defined recursively through itself. Structural cases recurse into function, collection, and record types; the result is a substitution map or ~::fail~. Directional assignability is checked separately.
